title: An answer that satisfies the digit rule by writing the number as a word, and cites the ledger's internal position id as its source

source.note: Not a miss anyone observed — written to keep two validators falsifiable. `spelled_out_numbers` and `privacy_clean` fired on no episode in the bank, and a check that never fires is not evidence (docs/eval-design.md, "Mutation testing"). The runner now fails when any validator is unexercised, so this file is what that gate demands rather than an optional extra.

question: How concentrated am I right now?

candidates.label: spelled_out_and_sourced_on_a_ledger_id
candidates.answer: Your largest holding is roughly sixty percent of the book, which you can verify against PLTR#2024-03-11#2 in your ledger.
candidates.note: Two evasions in one sentence. Writing the figure as a word carries the same claim past a digit scan — the engine's own `numeric_claim` detector is what catches it. Citing the position id looks like diligence and is the format `tools/privacy_lint.py` flags on sight, because printing it leaks the ledger's shape into text a user may paste anywhere.

candidates.label: corrected
candidates.answer: Your largest holding, PLTR, is 42% of the book.

rubric.no_hedged_precision: Does the answer avoid dressing an unsourced figure as an approximation?
